# Perception fixture images

Every image in this directory is drawn from nothing by
[`scripts/generate_perception_fixtures.py`](../../../../../scripts/generate_perception_fixtures.py)
and regenerated by `just perception-fixtures`. There is no photograph here, no
dataset, no third party with an interest, and nothing to check a licence against:
the provenance is the script, and it is committed beside them for exactly that
reason.

Regeneration is deterministic — every random draw is seeded — so a rerun that
changes a file means the drawing changed rather than the noise.

## What they are

| File | Contains |
|---|---|
| `face_single.jpg` | One drawn face, centred, 320×240 |
| `face_upper_left.jpg` | One drawn face in the upper-left quadrant, 320×240 |
| `face_pair.jpg` | Two drawn faces at different scales, 384×288 |
| `face_unaligned.jpg` | One drawn face, 300×220 — neither dimension a multiple of the model's stride |
| `scene_full.jpg` | A room with two people, 640×480 |
| `scene_half.jpg` | The same scene re-rendered at 320×240 |
| `negative_*.jpg` | Scenes with no face, no hand and no person |

`scene_full.jpg` and `scene_half.jpg` are two renderings of one scene rather than
one rendering resampled: every proportion in the drawing is a fraction of the
image, so the pair tests the detector's resolution independence rather than
OpenCV's resampler.

The `negative_*.jpg` set is the fixture set the gesture capability's
false-positive rate is measured against, and the set the face detector is
expected to find nothing in.

## What a drawn face proves

It proves the pipeline: that the model is fed correctly, that its heads are
decoded correctly, that overlapping candidates are suppressed correctly, and that
one scene at two resolutions reports the same place. The parity test in
particular compares two implementations over identical weights, so what the image
contains matters only in that it must make the model fire — a scene the model
ignored would compare zero detections against zero and pass having checked
nothing.

It proves nothing about accuracy on real faces. No image here is evidence about
how the detector behaves on a person; the WIDER Face figures quoted in the
perception spec are where that question is answered.
